review_candidates.title: Chief Technology Officer & Co-founder — Wider
review_candidates.description: Chief Technology Officer & Co-founder — Wider Candidate will apply using AI will be immediately rejected, the application has to be direct messages to Omar Hamdy's Inbox. Location:  Egypt (Cairo preferred)  Type:  Co-founder role; full-time; partially paid — a reduced cash salary balanced by meaningful equity  Reports to:  Founder (Omar Hamdy), working alongside co-founder Rakan Al Sulamy About Wider Wider is a group of companies built on one idea: integration creates possibility. Every organization is a set of circles, and Wider shortens the distances between them so integration becomes possible. The group today includes: Wider Labs  — AI delivery and engineering. Wider Labs moves AI development cost from overhead to cost of goods sold: customers pay as they receive value instead of funding a team upfront. Engagements start small and scale as the product proves itself. Wider Consulting  — the Saudi-registered parent entity that contracts with Gulf clients. Wider Community  — a MENA-focused business-integration ecosystem of partners, GLCs, ministries, and operators. Wider Labs ships on a set of ready-made product cores — Smart CRM, voice agents for business intelligence and operations, medical AI, advanced ASR, TTS/STT, and RAG — and commissions qualified clients to build, brand, and resell their own products on top of those cores. Underneath sits an orchestration engine that connects scenarios, stages, and objectives across every product surface. The team is run as a leadership center: concentric circles around the founder rather than a pyramid. Today, all technical direction flows through the founder. The CTO takes that seat. The role You will own Wider's technology end to end — architecture, engineering execution, the product cores, the orchestration layer, and the engineers who build them. You are not joining to manage a roadmap someone else wrote. You are joining to set the technical direction of a company that sells engineering as its product, and to make that engineering repeatable, sellable, and profitable. This is a co-founder seat. You carry founder-level accountability for outcomes, and you share in the upside. What you will own Technical direction and architecture Define and defend the architecture of the ready-made cores and the orchestration engine that connects them. Own the backend platform decisions, starting with the Java Spring Boot foundation already chosen, and decide what is built in-house versus delivered through partners. Keep the platform "agent-native": voice and chat as the primary surface, the full interface one toggle away, and the agent able to perform every action a human user can. Delivery engineering Turn client engagements into productized delivery: proven boilerplates, custom algorithms, and fine-tuned models where they earn their place. Own the token-economics work done with every customer — pricing sweet spot, cloud versus on-premise, data residency, MLOps requirements, and minimum hardware — so every solution is sustainable before it ships. Set engineering standards, review practices, and release discipline across all engagements. The Arsenal commissioning model Make the product cores genuinely reusable so a commissioned client receives a product they can own, brand, and resell within a predictable timeline and cost. Design the technical boundary between Wider's core and the client's product so both can evolve independently. Team and capability Lead the AI engineering, data engineering, and AI product management functions. Build the trainee-to-engineer pipeline that Wider depends on: the third circle of the team grows into the second under your direction. Become the single technical escalation point for the team, freeing the founder to focus on strategy, relationships, and growth. Domain infrastructure Provide technical stewardship for Wider's Arabic-language and governed-data work, including Quranic data infrastructure, where correctness, provenance, and governance are non-negotiable. Who we are looking for Technical depth gets you into the conversation. Leadership, communication, and delivery are what the role is actually about, and they are weighted above everything else in this list. Leadership A leader people follow because of who they are, not because of the title. You have built teams that outlasted your presence and developed engineers who went on to lead. Comfortable leading inside a leadership center rather than a hierarchy: you share direction with peers, hold your ground on technical calls, and give ground on everything else without keeping score. Able to hold two altitudes at once. You can set a multi-year technical vision that matches the size of the opportunity across the Gulf and Southeast Asia, and you can sit with a trainee at 11pm debugging a failed deployment without treating either as beneath you. You grow people deliberately. Wider's model depends on turning trainees into engineers and engineers into leaders, and you see that as core work, not a distraction from it. Communication You can explain a system architecture to a ministry director, a token-cost model to a CFO, and a code review to a first-year engineer, each in the language that lands. You write clearly and decisively. Decisions, trade-offs, and standards leave your hands documented and understood. You are steady in the room when things go wrong: a failed demo, an unhappy client, a missed date. You take responsibility in public and solve the problem in private. Fluent English is required; Arabic is a strong advantage given the client base. Delivery A track record of shipping production systems to real customers on committed dates, repeatedly, across multiple parallel engagements. You know how to break a large ambiguous engagement into a first small deliverable that proves value, and how to scale it from there without rebuilding. You treat sustainability as part of done: a system that works but costs too much to run is not finished. Soft skills at two levels This role demands enterprise-grade maturity and startup-grade grit at the same time, because Wider's clients are large institutions and Wider itself is still small. Enterprise level, to match the potential:  you carry yourself credibly with government, GLC, and large-corporate stakeholders. You understand procurement, governance, stakeholder management, and the patience long sales and delivery cycles require. Senior buyers trust you with their infrastructure. Startup level, to handle the day to day:  you are unbothered by ambiguity, thin resources, changing priorities, and doing work that is not in your job description. You make decisions with incomplete information, ship with what you have, and keep the team's energy up when the runway is the topic of conversation. The rare candidate holds both without switching modes: the same person who can run a steering committee can also run a three-person war room. Technical foundation Ten or more years building and shipping software, with at least three years leading engineering teams through production AI or ML delivery. Hands-on depth in LLM application architecture: retrieval systems, agent orchestration, evaluation, and cost control at the token level. Strong backend fundamentals, ideally on the JVM, and comfort making infrastructure decisions across cloud and on-premise environments. Experience delivering into regulated or governance-heavy environments where data residency and auditability matter. Strongly preferred Prior founder or early-employee experience at a services-to-product company. Familiarity with Gulf enterprise and government buyers, or Malaysian GLC environments. Speech technology experience (ASR, TTS) or Arabic NLP. Track record of productizing bespoke work into reusable cores. How we work Decisions are made in short, frequent rhythms: a daily directive meeting, leader check-ins twice a week, and a weekly retrospective with a decision log and weekly targets. Technical matters route to the CTO. Administrative and interpersonal matters route to the team manager and co-founder responsible for relationships. This separation is deliberate and protects your focus. We lead through a shared story and a small set of principles, referenced lightly rather than imposed. Survival belongs to the fittest, not the strongest. Leadership sessions are recorded and published. Expect to be visible. What we offer Meaningful co-founder equity, negotiated on the basis of stage, contribution, and commitment. Equity is the primary reward in this role. A partial cash salary, below market for the Egyptian tech sector, that covers living costs while the company scales. The cash component is reviewed as revenue grows, with a defined path to a full market salary. A choice in how the balance is struck: a candidate who prefers more cash and less equity, or the reverse, can propose the split that fits their situation. Direct access to a live client base across Saudi Arabia and Malaysia, and a partner-led sales channel that sources engagements so you can focus on delivery. The mandate to shape a company's technology from its foundation rather than inherit it. How to apply Send a short note covering two things: one system you designed that had to stay economically sustainable in production and the trade-offs you made, and one time you led a team through a period where the plan fell apart, what you did, and what the team looked like afterwards. Include links to work where possible. A CV is welcome but the note matters more.
